Directive:
 pH Meter SyberScan 500
Introduction

The CyberScan pH 500 series 
 bench pH meter measure the 
 pH in a solution. pH is a measure of relative acidity or alkalinity of water; 
 so, it is a most important factor influencing scaleforming and corrosion 
 tendencies.

The first draft was 
 initiated by chemist: Mohammed Eshra, Reviewed by chemical general director: 
 Aness Abou Al Ezz, Revised by quality control chemist: Wael A. Tantawy, and 
 accepted By Eng. Mohammed Hamoda Al Sarag, the Head Sector of Damietta Power 
 Station.
Information
General

Solution pH is a 
measure of the active acid or base in a solution.

pH is defined as the negative 
logarithm of the hydrogen ion concentration.

Neutral water has (7) 
values, below (7) approaching (0) are increasingly acid while values above 
(7-14) are increasingly basic.

Low pH water increases 
the potential for corrosion of equipment.

High pH water can cause 
precipitation of calcium carbonate on the surfaces of pipelines, heat 
exchangers, condensers and other components.

In clarification processes, 
pH is an important determination, the control of coagulation is optimized through 
pH control because every coagulant possesses an optimum pH range in which it 
provides the most efficient performance.

The pH value of boiler 
water is usually adjusted to control both depositions and corrosion.

Electrometric determination of the pH of a solution involves 
the measurement of the electromotive force (EMF) of a cell comprising an 
indicator electrode.

An electrode responsive to 
hydrogen ions such as a glass electrode immersed in the test solution and 
reference electrode.

These electrode systems are 
potentiometric devices and when connected with a suitable reference electrode to 
form an electrochemical cell give voltage out puts related to the activity of 
the (H+) ion concentration according to Nernist Equation.

The voltage output is 
proportional logarithm of the ion activity.

sections.text: Calibration Procedure

pH Calibration 
Procedure ( with ATC )

It is recommended to perform 
at least 2-point calibration using standard buffers.

1-point calibration can also 
be used for quick measurements.

The instrument is capable of 
multipoint calibration (up to maximum of 3 points) to ensure enhanced 
accuracy throughout the pH measurement range (pH 4.01 , 7.00 and 10.0 ).

To activate the Automatic 
Temperature Compensation (ATC), simply plug in the temperature probe into phono 
jack.

Directives

Maintenance 
of the pH Meter SyberScan 500
Electrode Maintenance

pH electrodes are susceptible 
to dirt and contamination and need to be cleaned regularly

depending on the 
extent and condition of use.
Storage

Always keep the pH bulb wet in pH 4 buffer with (1/100) part of saturated KCl. 
Other pH buffers or tap water are also acceptable storage media, but avoid storage in de-ionized water.

The protective rubber cap filled with the buffer solution provides storage for 
long periods.

Electrolyte 
Replacement (for Refillable Electrodes only)

The reference electrolyte 
needs to be refilled when the electrode has been 
used for an extended period, or when the internal electrolyte has dried up.

To accomplish this, follow the procedure detailed 
below.

1. Remove the protective rubber cap or sleeve to expose the filling port of the 
electrode. Remove the old reference electrolyte with a syringe and a flexible tube.

2. Fill the new reference electrolyte with (3M KCl) until reaches the 
level of the refilling port. Replace the Rubber Sleeve.
3. Rinse the electrolyte with de-ionized water and tap dry.

Electrode 
Cleaning

Salt 
Deposits

Dissolve the deposit by immersing the electrode in tap water for 1015 minutes, 
then thoroughly rinse with deionized water.

Oil / Grease 
Films

Wash electrode pH bulb in a little detergent and water. Rinse 
electrode tip with deionized water.
Clogged Reference Junction
Heat a dilute KCL solution to 6080oC.

Place the sensing portion of the pH electrode into the heated 
KCL solution for approximately 10 minutes.

Allow the electrode to cool while immersed in some unheated 
KCL solution.

sections.text:
Electrode 
Activation

Generally if the procedure of the storage and maintenance had 
been closely followed, the electrode can be used immediately.

However, should the electrode response become sluggish, it may 
be possible that the bulb has dehydrated.

The bulb can be re-hydrated by immersing the electrode in an 
ideal storage solution (e.g. buffer pH 4 solution) for 1-2 hours.
If this fails the electrode may require re-activation.

At no time should one touch or rub the glass at this cause the 
buildup of electrostatic charge.

If the above procedure does not re-activate the electrode to 
acceptable status, try rejuvenating the electrode by following the procedure 
outlined below.

sections.text:
Rejuvenation 
Procedure

Dip and stir the electrode in rejuvenation procedure freon or 
alcohol for 5 minutes.
Leave the electrode in tap water for 15 minutes.

Dip and stir the electrode in concentrated acid (e.g. HCl, H2 
SO4) for 5 minutes.
Repeat step 2.
Dip and stir in strong base NaOH for 5 minutes.
Leave for 15 minutes in tap water.

Test with standard calibration buffer solution to see if the 
electrode yields acceptable results.
